stem: An overweight 13-year-old is assessed after hyperglycaemia is found, and examination shows acanthosis nigricans with a strong family history of diabetes; which type of diabetes should be considered?
explanation: Type 2 diabetes mellitus should be considered because obesity, acanthosis nigricans, and a strong family history are classic features that fit this presentation.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diabetes in Children and Adolescents

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this presentation is more suggestive of type 2 diabetes than type 1 diabetes.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because obesity, acanthosis nigricans, and a strong family history are classic features that should prompt consideration of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because monogenic diabetes is not the best fit for this phenotype of obesity and acanthosis nigricans.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because there is no medication history suggesting drug-induced hyperglycaemia, and this is not the best match.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because diabetes should be considered in this clinical setting given the hyperglycaemia and associated features.
